title: Rapid Onramp: Security Prioritization Ladder for Customer Data Classifications and Questionnaire Routing
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Define a pragmatic, deterministic prioritization ladder (onramp) for incoming enterprise security & compliance requests tied to customer data classifications and questionnaire types (SOC2/ISO attestations, HIPAA, GDPR/DPA, vendor questionnaires). This ticket scopes the decision matrix, routing lanes, SLA commitments, and a lightweight evidence-bundling recommendation to reduce back-and-forth for high-touch accounts.

Problem statement: Enterprise customers submit a mix of security questionnaires, audit requests, and residency/DPA asks. Current intake is ad-hoc and burdens Legal/Security because triage lacks consistent signals (data classification, risk appetite, contract stage). That leads to inconsistent SLAs, duplicate work, and missed escalation paths for high-risk accounts.

Proposed solution:
1) Data classification-first scoring: Each incoming ask is annotated with a primary data classification (Public, Internal, Confidential, Regulated). The score ladder maps classification + request type -> priority lane. Example: Regulated + HIPAA request or DPA with data-flow ask => High (Tier 1). Confidential + SOC2 questionnaire => Medium (Tier 2).
2) Questionnaire fingerprinting: Automatically detect common questionnaire templates (SIG, CAIQ, VendorSecurityQuestionnaire) and extract high-risk sections (data residency, encryption/KMS, processing subprocessors). Use a short heuristic parser to pre-fill checklist items and surface to triage team.
3) Deterministic routing lanes: Triage lanes: Auto-Respond (low/no PII, standard templates), Evidence-Collector (standard but missing attachments), Security-Review (high-risk or legal clauses flagged), Legal-Escalation (contract-level DPA exceptions). Each lane has a target SLA and owner group.
4) Onramp ladder: Define 4 tiers with explicit SLAs and deliverable expectations: Tier 0 (Auto/Low) 5 business days, Tier 1 (High/Regulated) 2 business days initial response + 10 business days evidence package, Tier 2 (Medium) 7 business days, Tier 3 (Backlog/Low-priority) 20 business days.
5) Evidence bundling template: Provide a prebuilt evidence pack per lane (SOC2 summary + docs link, encryption/KMS statements, data flow diagram template, contractual clauses mapping) and a checklist for Solutions/SEs to attach before escalation.

Acceptance criteria:
- Decision matrix (classification + request type -> tier) documented and agreed by Security & Legal.
- Routing lanes configured in intake tool with owners and SLA fields.
- Parser prototype that identifies at least 3 common questionnaire templates and extracts residency/encryption/processors fields with >70% precision on a 50-sample set.
- Evidence bundling templates for Tier 1 and Tier 2 tested with two internal playbook runs.
- Playbook and sample responses published in Confluence, with a one-pager for Solutions team.

Trade-offs & notes:
- We prefer deterministic rules over ML triage initially to keep auditing simple; can iterate to model-based scoring after 2 quarters.
- Parser will rely on heuristics and regexes for now; engineering estimate assumes 2 weeks of effort for proof-of-concept.
- Some customers will still require bespoke legal negotiation; this ladder aims to reduce volume of those asks, not eliminate them.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1: Align Security & Legal on classification taxonomy and initial decision matrix.
- Week 2: Build parser prototype and routing configuration in intake tool; draft evidence templates.
- Week 3: Pilot with Solutions/SE on 10 live accounts.
- Week 4: Collect feedback, iterate thresholds, and publish playbook.

Links and artifacts: Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Sec/Onramp-Decision-Ladder, Parser prototype repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sec-intake-parser (PR pending), Sample evidence pack (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/example-evidence-pack
